title: The Situation in Ukraine and its Implications
what_it_is: The Situation in Ukraine and its Implications

sections.label: Ukraine nuclear arsenal and Budapest Memorandum
sections.summary: Ukraine gave up its nuclear arsenal in 1994 via the Non-Proliferation Treaty, and Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 despite the Budapest Memorandum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter in 1994, Ukraine was persuaded to give up its nuclear arsenal, at that time the third largest in the world, by signing on to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In return, Russia, the US and the UK, via the Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances, "reaffirmed their obligation to refrain from the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of Ukraine, and that none of their weapons will ever be used against Ukraine except in self-defence or otherwise in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations (UN)" – words which perhaps ring quite hollow today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Twenty years after the Budapest Memorandum, Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 whilst the world watched.

sections.label: Russia's invasion violates international norms
sections.summary: Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a clear and gross violation of international norms and an unacceptable precedent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine is a clear and gross violation of the international norms and a completely unacceptable precedent.

sections.label: Singapore condemns Russia's attack
sections.summary: Singapore must take violations of core principles seriously and has strongly condemned Russia's unprovoked attack on Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore must take any violation of these core principles seriously, whenever and wherever they occur.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And this is why Singapore has strongly condemned Russia's unprovoked attack on Ukraine.

sections.label: Singapore's defence and National Service
sections.summary: Singapore must defend itself, so it has invested in a credible SAF and maintained National Service as fundamental to nationhood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Thus, we must never lose the ability to defend and look after ourselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And this is why Singapore has invested consistently to build up a credible and strong SAF and to maintain National Service as a fundamental element of our nationhood.

sections.label: Singapore sanctions against Russia
sections.summary: Singapore intends to impose sanctions and restrictions on Russia, including export controls and blocking certain banks and financial transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore has always complied fully with sanctions and decisions of the UNSC, but we have rarely acted to impose sanctions on other countries in the absence of binding Security Council decisions or directions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, given the unprecedented gravity of the Russian attack on Ukraine and the unsurprising veto by Russia of a draft UNSC resolution, Singapore intends to act in concert with many other like-minded countries to impose appropriate sanctions and restrictions against Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In particular, we will impose export controls on items that can be used directly as weapons in Ukraine to inflict harm or to subjugate the Ukrainians.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will also block certain Russian banks and financial transactions connected to Russia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We must expect that our measures will come at some cost and implications on our businesses, citizens and indeed to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, unless we as a country stand up for principles that are the very foundation for the independence and sovereignty of smaller nations, our own right to exist and prosper as a nation may similarly be called into question one day.

sections.label: Singaporeans leaving and in Ukraine
sections.summary: Seven Singaporeans left Ukraine before the conflict, three more left since the invasion, and eight remain in Ukraine with MFA in contact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Following our first Travel Advisory, seven Singaporeans left Ukraine via commercial options before the conflict erupted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the Russian invasion, another three Singaporeans have left Ukraine and made their way across the border into Poland.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are still in touch with eight Singaporeans currently in Ukraine who are spread across several cities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are aware of at least one other person whom we are still trying to contact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: MFA has been in contact with them, and we will assist them wherever and however possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are also exploring options for them to leave the country if the situation permits.

sections.label: Principles of independence and sovereignty
sections.summary: The Member says Singapore does not take sides but upholds principles of independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Member's questions on balance, I would address by bringing us back to first principles: that we do not take sides, we uphold principles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And in this case, the principles at stake are independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

sections.label: No others shed blood
sections.summary: The passage states that nobody else will shed blood on our account.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Nobody else will shed blood on our account.

sections.label: Price of standing on principle
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore stands on principle and may pay a price, worth paying for its future existence, independence and prosperity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In the larger point I am making, is that, yes, we are standing on principle, and yes, we may even have to pay a price, but this is a price worth paying for the future existence, independence and prosperity of Singapore.

sections.label: Support for international law and UN
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore is a staunch supporter of international law and the United Nations, the alternative being might is right.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As I have said, that is why we are such staunch supporters of international law and the United Nations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We have to be, because the alternative is "might is right" or the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must.

sections.label: Red Cross, Government and ASEAN contributions
sections.summary: The passage states the Singapore Red Cross gave US$100,000, the Singapore Government will contribute, and ASEAN took a stand on territorial integrity and sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: He is right; the virus and violence are a perfect recipe of humanitarian disaster, which is occurring right now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I explained earlier in my statement that the Singapore Red Cross has contributed US$100,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Singapore Government will also contribute to that and I am sure members of the public will also be generous.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: At the ASEAN level, ASEAN has taken a stand that there needs to be mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty.

sections.label: Danger of abrogating international law
sections.summary: The passage states the abrogation of international law and norms is a clear and present danger, especially for small states like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The abrogation of international law and norms is a clear and present danger especially for small states like us and that is why we have had to take such a principled stand.

sections.label: Standing for norms and borders
sections.summary: Non-compliance with norms and trifling with borders makes a more dangerous world, so Singapore takes a stand for its long-term survival, prosperity and peace.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The point is if norms are not complied with and if borders can be trifled with, on the basis of all kinds of justifications and sometimes even pretext, then it will be a much more dangerous world, and especially for us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, bear in mind that, actually, we are taking a stand not just for this particular crisis, but we are taking a stand for our long-term survival, prosperity and peace.

sections.label: Refugees and population density
sections.summary: ICA and MHA would look at the matter, and Singapore reiterates it cannot take refugees as it is one of the most dense states.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This is something which ICA and MHA would look at and I am not in a position to give any blanket assurances on that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think I will also have to reiterate our long-held position that we cannot take refugees because we are one of the most dense cities or states in the world.

sections.label: Foreign politics and armed groups
sections.summary: Singapore does not allow import of foreign politics into its domestic environment and cannot support promotion or organisation of armed groups into other countries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore does not allow the import of foreign politics into Singapore's domestic environment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Similarly, Singapore cannot support the promotion or organisation of armed groups, whatever their justification, into other countries.

sections.label: Foreign ministers in contact
sections.summary: All the foreign ministers and officials have been in intensive contact over the last few days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The short answer to that is yes, all the foreign ministers and our officials have been in intensive contact over the last few days.
